method: Dedicated app-owned ordinary Chrome on macOS, official public award form and normal Money/Miles controls; no login, imported browser state or direct inventory replay.

approvedDecisionRule.decision: Switch early to an operator-account pilot because both tested award entry sequences explicitly require membership.

observations.result: Official form accepted the route/date/party and opened the sign-in dialog before award inventory. No available native award fares observed.

Page displayed its non-dismissible Continue shopping dialog explaining that miles results require sign-in. Offered controls: cash results, sign-in, homepage. An attempted Update click was intercepted by this visible modal; it is not classified as an airline denial.

Real cash flight rows loaded, including UA1625 and UA1496 nonstop LAX-AUS and connecting itineraries. Example UA1625 Economy from USD159; this is a cash observation, not an award value or full fare audit.

observations.action: Select Miles in the actual Show price in dropdown and click Update.
observations.result: Sign-in opened again; no new award inventory request observed.
The same explicit miles-requires-sign-in dialog reappeared. Cash initialization did not unlock anonymous native awards.

findings: The award continuation dialog is configured as non-dismissible and offers revenue continuation, sign-in and homepage actions.
Generic continue-as-guest copy exists elsewhere in delivered code, but no award guest continuation was visible in either actual tested flow.
publicCodeEvidence.limit: Client-flow and visible-page evidence; not a proof that every possible backend or future anonymous path is unavailable.

decision.next: Authorized operator-account pilot: user signs in directly in the dedicated United browser; first establish two genuine native award queries before attempting integration or extended recovery.

privacy: No credentials, codes, cookies or authorization headers are included in this evidence. Public source code is identified by URL and digest rather than redistributed.
